locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in how this consumer receives, processes, and acknowledges messages? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: There is none. Messages are acked only after send succeeds, so a crash mid-send leads to redelivery, and the sender gets notificationId as an idempotency key so redelivery does not double-notify. In-flight work is bounded by maxInFlight: the loop only requests the remaining capacity and waits on Promise.race when full. Transient failures extend visibility with capped exponential backoff, permanent or exhausted ones go to the DLQ, and the original is acked only after the DLQ send succeeds. stop() ends polling, then waits for in-flight handlers before returning.

choiceQuestions.prompt: The process crashes after sender.send succeeds but before ack completes. What happens?
choices: The message becomes visible again and is redelivered; the idempotency key lets the sender avoid a duplicate notification
The message goes straight to the dead-letter queue
The queue acks it automatically because the handler started
choiceQuestions.explanation: Without an ack the queue redelivers after the visibility timeout. send is called with idempotencyKey: job.notificationId so a repeat can be deduplicated downstream. Nothing is lost, nothing routes to the DLQ on a crash, and the queue never auto-acks.

choiceQuestions.prompt: With maxInFlight = 10 and 10 handlers currently running, what does the poll loop do?
choices: Receives up to 10 more messages anyway
Waits for any one in-flight handler to finish, then receives only as many messages as there is free capacity
choiceQuestions.explanation: capacity is 0, so it awaits Promise.race(this.inFlight), which resolves when any handler settles (tasks remove themselves in finally), then recomputes capacity. It never exceeds the limit, never calls receive with 0, and does not wait for all handlers.

choiceQuestions.prompt: A message fails transiently on its 3rd delivery with baseRetryDelaySec = 30 and maxAttempts = 5. What happens?
choices: It is made invisible for 120 seconds before the next delivery
It is acked and re-sent as a new message
choiceQuestions.explanation: receiveCount 3 is below maxAttempts, so the backoff is 30 * 2^(3-1) = 120 seconds (under the 900 cap) and visibility is changed accordingly. Dead-lettering needs a permanent error or receiveCount >= 5, there is no re-send, and there is no in-process retry.
